answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a locking escrow: voting weight equals the slashable stake an agent posts, frozen until the decision horizon passes. Auditors sample ballots at random, and proof that two votes share one controller burns both stakes. The auditor is a falcon that strikes any ballot without warning, so duplicates cannot be parked where checks are unlikely. Minting k fake agents needs k bonds locked, and expected forfeiture exceeds what the extra votes could buy. A zephyr of new accounts gives no cheap win: capital stays frozen and is seized, so the raid costs more than it pays.
